title: What CONDITIONING really is
hook: A plain Python list. Each entry is a tensor and a dict. Nearly every conditioning node just changes one of those, and that explains what they can and can't do.

verified.claim: encode_from_tokens_scheduled returns a list of [cond tensor, dict], with pooled_output in the dict.
conditioning_set_values copies each dict and shares each tensor.
Combine, SetArea, SetTimestepRange and Concat, run as the real nodes on a CPU, give these shapes and keys.
convert_cond turns each entry into a dict with cross_attn, model_conds and uuid.
The dict's keys reach the model through extra_conds as keyword arguments, and a class reads only the ones it looks for.
SD 1.5's tensor has width 768, from the config's hidden_size.

unchecked: The lab uses random tensors with the real shapes. It didn't load a text encoder.
We list keys used by the nodes in this track, not every key in core.
